claims.text: The complex multi-element configuration of lightweight HEAs induces pronounced lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion stabilizes a network of nanoscale precipitates.
The lattice-distortion-stabilized precipitates are coherent and uniformly distributed.
Near-equiatomic distribution of multiple elements promotes the nucleation and stabilization of nanoscale precipitates.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates hinder dislocation motion.
Hindering dislocation motion through the precipitate network enhances mechanical strength.
The precipitate network blocks oxygen diffusion pathways and thereby improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The precipitate network blocks diffusion of corrosive ions and thereby improves corrosion resistance.
Lightweight HEAs can exhibit a combination of low density, high mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
An amorphous AlTiVNb HEA film can be fabricated by magnetron sputtering.
The sputtered AlTiVNb film has a homogeneous amorphous or highly disordered structure.
The initial AlTiVNb material is a homogeneous solid solution containing pre-nucleated nanoscale coherent precipitates.
Relative to a conventional baseline alloy, the lightweight HEA will have a finer and more stable precipitate distribution.
Relative to a similar-density conventional baseline alloy, the lightweight HEA will have higher compressive strength.
Relative to the conventional baseline alloy, the lightweight HEA will have a lower corrosion rate.
Relative to the conventional baseline alloy, the lightweight HEA will have a lower high-temperature oxidation rate.
A conventional alloy lacking the complex multi-element design will have larger and less uniformly distributed precipitates.
Thermally activated precipitate coarsening will eliminate the nanoscale barrier effect and end the simultaneous mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation benefits.
Phase segregation will eliminate the nanoscale barrier effect and end the simultaneous mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation benefits.

contradictions.description: The material is described as a homogeneous amorphous structure while also containing a network of coherent precipitates. Crystallographic coherency requires an ordered lattice relationship, which is not defined for a homogeneous amorphous matrix.

The initial state already contains pre-nucleated precipitates, whereas the hypothesis attributes their induction and stabilization to the multi-element configuration without specifying when or how they form.
